- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (sentiment < 0.2) — add 3–7% to forecast to compensate for mean reversion.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes — cap forecast 3–5 days after spike at 10–15% below peak.
- Lagged mean reversion: if sentiment turns negative after 3–5 days, forecast should trend downward 2–4% per day.
- Avoid overconfidence in 30-day horizon — reduce forecast by 2–5% if sentiment is neutral or declining.
- If sentiment is rising but price is falling, adjust forecast downward by 1–3% to avoid “sentiment mismatch”.
- Use sentiment as a volatility filter — if sentiment > 0.7, reduce forecast variance by 10–20% to avoid over-optimism.
